report: Reviewed the complete invocation claim, its one ordinary implementation entry in compile/mod.rs, and both ordinary associated tests; no TODO or N/A entries exist. Requirements: an invocation runs in an ordinary Rust #[test] with standard Cargo discovery; fixture sources are expressions; explicit expect_test expectations stay at the invocation; existing #[sage::test(...)] associations suffice; an observation mismatch fails the Rust test. The exported compile_test macro expands to a block that constructs CompileTest, dispatches expr-valued fields (including source and Expect values), and calls run synchronously. It neither registers a custom harness nor discovers tests. source accepts AsRef<str>; expectation setters accept Expect; run propagates preparation failures by panic and calls assert_eq on each requested observation, diagnostic, or query expectation without swallowing failure. All invocation-specific implementation is in the associated whole-file snapshot. Captured Cargo.toml confirms normal integration-test discovery with no harness=false override. The complete call_argument_types test has ordinary #[test] and the existing sage association, passes an indoc expression and literal expect values directly to compile_test, and asserts three precise rendered types plus empty diagnostics. This exercises source expression acceptance, call-site assertions, and regular harness invocation. The complete blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates test creates a disposable ordinary Cargo package containing a plain #[test] that calls compile_test with inline source/expect values, runs cargo test, requires failure for stale observations with UPDATE_EXPECT absent, verifies the failure is specifically 'expect test failed', then updates the expectation and requires the same test to pass with updating disabled. Its status assertion and diagnostic check distinguish behavioral assertion failure from compilation failure. The unexpected-diagnostic branch additionally confirms preparation failures propagate. This test would catch dropped observation assertions or swallowed panics. Explicit blessing mode is separately specified and intentionally converts stale representations into updated expectations; normal observation mismatches fail. Additional captured context is the crate manifest and review workflow specification. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests call_argument_types -- --exact (one passed) and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test callsite_updates blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates -- --exact (one passed). Existing unrelated compiler warnings were emitted. No production or test edits were made. Source inspection and both executed tests account for all parts of this anchor; no edits requested.
